requirement.evidence: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
requirement.note: The nonpayment threshold of one month of FMR in the Oakland-Fremont HUD Metro FMR is also stated in the document.

key_value.evidence: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR

effective_date.note: Field is empty on the card.

status.evidence: Eviction for nonpayment of rent is no longer permitted for rental debt of less than one month’s Fair Market Rent for a unit of equivalent size.
status.note: Document presents the rule as current law.

coverage.note: Field is empty on the card.

citation.evidence: Measure BB, a ballot measure passed by Berkeley voters in the November 2024 election, makes several changes to Berkeley’s Rent Ordinance
citation.note: Measure BB and the Nov 2024 election are supported, but the document never names the 'Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance' by that title.

requirement.evidence: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%. This cap does not prevent a landlord who has “banked” (unused) AGAs from previous years from implementing a rent increase that is greater than 5% in order to raise the rent to the rent ceiling.

key_value.evidence: The elected Rent Board sets the AGA by following a formula in the Rent Ordinance that ties the AGA to the Consumer Price Index.
key_value.note: Maximum 5% is stated in the document.
